texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Livestock
texts.text: Livestock

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Hay supplies are generally adequate with some producers expecting carry-over. Hay is still available for sale for producers who may need to top up their feed supplies.
texts.text: Hay supplies are generally adequate with some producers expecting carry-over. Hay is still available for sale for producers who may need to top up their feed supplies.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Cattle remain in their winter-feeding areas. Some operations have opened smaller paddocks adjacent to corrals; allowing animals more space. Corrals are dry and animals are comfortable. This is fortunate as grass on pasture could use more time to green-up and for growth.
texts.text: Cattle remain in their winter-feeding areas. Some operations have opened smaller paddocks adjacent to corrals; allowing animals more space. Corrals are dry and animals are comfortable. This is fortunate as grass on pasture could use more time to green-up and for growth.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Producers are checking fence-lines and prepping for the eventual move of cattle to pasture.
texts.text: Producers are checking fence-lines and prepping for the eventual move of cattle to pasture.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Some herds are being turned out to stockpiled grass, with most sites still requiring supplementation. Turning animals out too early could decrease pasture growth over the season, especially with current drier conditions.
texts.text: Some herds are being turned out to stockpiled grass, with most sites still requiring supplementation. Turning animals out too early could decrease pasture growth over the season, especially with current drier conditions.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Recent winds and heat have reduced the amount of standing water, however most dugouts are full, and some creeks are still running. Most water sources for livestock are adequate, however lower than normal levels are being reported for the Pas and Swan River.
texts.text: Recent winds and heat have reduced the amount of standing water, however most dugouts are full, and some creeks are still running. Most water sources for livestock are adequate, however lower than normal levels are being reported for the Pas and Swan River.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Pasture and hay fields are slowly greening up and showing minimal growth with previously overgrazed pastures further behind. Some producers are starting to talk about the possibility of dry conditions. Warm weather and some spotty showers last week brought on good growth in pastures and hay land in southern Manitoba.
texts.text: Pasture and hay fields are slowly greening up and showing minimal growth with previously overgrazed pastures further behind. Some producers are starting to talk about the possibility of dry conditions. Warm weather and some spotty showers last week brought on good growth in pastures and hay land in southern Manitoba.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Regional Comments
texts.text: Regional Comments

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Southwest
texts.text: Southwest

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Good weather over the past week has given producers an opportunity to accelerate their seeding operations. Most of the seeding activity has occurred in the southern parts of the region, although there has been some in northern areas including Rivers, Oak River, and Rapid City. Overall, seedbed conditions are good, and soil moisture is at an optimal level across most of the region.
texts.text: Good weather over the past week has given producers an opportunity to accelerate their seeding operations. Most of the seeding activity has occurred in the southern parts of the region, although there has been some in northern areas including Rivers, Oak River, and Rapid City. Overall, seedbed conditions are good, and soil moisture is at an optimal level across most of the region.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Producers are also applying fertilizers and pre-seed burn-off herbicides, although windy conditions are hindering progress in some areas. Weeds are beginning to emerge as temperatures continue to rise. Winter wheat and fall rye are coming out of dormancy and are looking healthy.
texts.text: Producers are also applying fertilizers and pre-seed burn-off herbicides, although windy conditions are hindering progress in some areas. Weeds are beginning to emerge as temperatures continue to rise. Winter wheat and fall rye are coming out of dormancy and are looking healthy.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Northwest
texts.text: Northwest

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Spring operations are underway, with seeding having a good start in most areas of the Northwest region. Spring wheat seeding has begun across most of the region, apart from The Pas, which is anticipated to begin this week. Fertilizer application and harrowing are also ongoing.
texts.text: Spring operations are underway, with seeding having a good start in most areas of the Northwest region. Spring wheat seeding has begun across most of the region, apart from The Pas, which is anticipated to begin this week. Fertilizer application and harrowing are also ongoing.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Wildfires in The Pas are a concern. Many other locations across the region are high risk and have a burn ban in place.
texts.text: Wildfires in The Pas are a concern. Many other locations across the region are high risk and have a burn ban in place.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Fall rye and winter wheat continue to look good.
texts.text: Fall rye and winter wheat continue to look good.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Central
texts.text: Central

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Favourable weather over the past week has allowed significant progress in field operations across the Central Region. These conditions, especially the high winds over the weekend, have helped many fields dry sufficiently to support machinery and early-season activities.
texts.text: Favourable weather over the past week has allowed significant progress in field operations across the Central Region. These conditions, especially the high winds over the weekend, have helped many fields dry sufficiently to support machinery and early-season activities.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Most producers have begun some form of field operations, while a small number are still completing final equipment checks, calibration, and maintenance. Substantial progress has been made in the seeding of cereals and peas, with the earliest established pea and cereal crops emerging. A few producers have also started seeding canola, sunflowers, soybean and corn, encouraged by warm soil temperatures and a favourable forecast. Potato planting is underway.
texts.text: Most producers have begun some form of field operations, while a small number are still completing final equipment checks, calibration, and maintenance. Substantial progress has been made in the seeding of cereals and peas, with the earliest established pea and cereal crops emerging. A few producers have also started seeding canola, sunflowers, soybean and corn, encouraged by warm soil temperatures and a favourable forecast. Potato planting is underway.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Winter wheat and fall rye are growing rapidly, and most producers have completed fertilizer applications on these winter cereals. Winter cereal survival is generally good, with most producers reporting 80 to 90 percent survival.
texts.text: Winter wheat and fall rye are growing rapidly, and most producers have completed fertilizer applications on these winter cereals. Winter cereal survival is generally good, with most producers reporting 80 to 90 percent survival.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Eastern
texts.text: Eastern

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Fields were dry enough for general manure/fertilizer applications and seeding this past week. Spring wheat seeding has moved forward quickly, with other crops including oats, barley, and corn also being planted. Canola and sunflower acres will be next , with producers factoring in warm soil temperatures in the top inch and flea beetle control efficacy.
texts.text: Fields were dry enough for general manure/fertilizer applications and seeding this past week. Spring wheat seeding has moved forward quickly, with other crops including oats, barley, and corn also being planted. Canola and sunflower acres will be next , with producers factoring in warm soil temperatures in the top inch and flea beetle control efficacy.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A few soybean acres have been planted but it is expected that planting will become more general this week as growers finish up their cereal crops. The field pea acres are close to being completed, with the earliest planted fields beginning to emerge.
texts.text: A few soybean acres have been planted but it is expected that planting will become more general this week as growers finish up their cereal crops. The field pea acres are close to being completed, with the earliest planted fields beginning to emerge.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Interlake
texts.text: Interlake

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Seeding across the Interlake region is well underway particularly in the South with the recent weather conditions. The North Interlake region has just begun seeding spring cereals. Overall, seeding of spring cereals is the most advanced across the region, with soybeans, peas, canola, and silage corn to be seeded next. The soil temperature at 2" depth was over 7 degrees with good soil moisture, so seeding will most likely advance quickly.
texts.text: Seeding across the Interlake region is well underway particularly in the South with the recent weather conditions. The North Interlake region has just begun seeding spring cereals. Overall, seeding of spring cereals is the most advanced across the region, with soybeans, peas, canola, and silage corn to be seeded next. The soil temperature at 2" depth was over 7 degrees with good soil moisture, so seeding will most likely advance quickly.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Winter cereal fertilizer applications are close to being done except for a few wet fields. Winter cereal and fall rye survival looks very promising with field conditions ranging from fair to good. Volunteer canola has started to emerge.
texts.text: Winter cereal fertilizer applications are close to being done except for a few wet fields. Winter cereal and fall rye survival looks very promising with field conditions ranging from fair to good. Volunteer canola has started to emerge.
